the world is becoming more eco-efficient at producing four important crops, and that this is occurring in a way that is consistent with the global imperative of increasing production while reducing the ecological impacts of agriculture.

the world's most important crops are becoming more eco-efficient, with the greatest gains in the high-intensification production regions, and that the low-intensified production regions have not yet achieved the same levels of eco-efficient production as their high-intensified counterparts.

(1) high-intensification production systems are the most eco-efficient, (2) eco-efficiency is improving in high- and medium-production-intensification countries but not in low-production-intensification systems, and (3) the most eco-efficient production systems have the highest yields.

the sustainability of the world's agricultural systems, and our results suggest a strong link between intensification and eco-efficiency gains.
